items.title: extract_content fails with "'NoneType' object is not callable" when beautifulsoup4 is absent
items.body:
## Summary

`InternetSearch.extract_content()` fails with `'NoneType' object is not callable`
when `beautifulsoup4` is not installed. The module degrades an `ImportError` into a
`None` binding and then calls it, so a missing dependency surfaces as a meaningless
runtime error attributed to the page being fetched.

## Reproduction

In an environment without `beautifulsoup4` (for example a
`jarviscore-framework[redis,typesafe]` install):

```python
from jarviscore.search.internet_search import InternetSearch

fresh = InternetSearch()
result = await fresh.extract_content("https://www.gov.uk/prepare-file-annual-accounts-for-limited-company")
```

Observed:

```
Unexpected error fetching https://www.gov.uk/prepare-file-annual-accounts-for-limited-company: 'NoneType' object is not callable
{'url': 'https://www.gov.uk/prepare-file-annual-accounts-for-limited-company',
 'error': "'NoneType' object is not callable",
 'error_type': 'PROCESSING',
 'content_length': '0'}
```

Reproduced on a fresh client and after a successful `search()`, so it is not session
state. The HTTP fetch succeeds; the failure is in processing.

## Cause

`jarviscore/search/internet_search.py`:

```python
try:
    from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
except ImportError:
    BeautifulSoup = None  # type: ignore[assignment,misc]
```

then later, in the HTML branch of `extract_content`:

```python
soup = BeautifulSoup(html, 'html.parser')
```

`beautifulsoup4>=4.12.0` is declared only in the `web` and `research` extras, so any
install that does not pull one of those hits this on the first page fetch. The
`error_type` is reported as `PROCESSING`, which points a caller at the target page
rather than at their own environment.

## Expected

Name the missing capability, in the style of the TypeSafe guard in
`jarviscore/execution/decisions.py`:

```python
raise DecisionClientError(
    'TypeSafe support requires `pip install "jarviscore-framework[typesafe]"`.'
)
```

Something equivalent at import or first use, for example
`Page extraction requires pip install "jarviscore-framework[research]"`, would make
this self-diagnosing. Returning `error_type: "MISSING_DEPENDENCY"` rather than
`PROCESSING` would also let callers distinguish an environment problem from a bad page.

## Workaround

Declaring `beautifulsoup4>=4.12,<5` directly in the consuming project fixes it. After
installing it, the same URL extracted in 0.9s into 7 segments.

## Related

Same family as #121 (empty LLM provider chain fails with `Last error: None` instead of
naming the misconfiguration).

Found while dogfooding JarvisCore for capital-markets external evidence capture.
macOS, Python 3.12.

items.title: [Week 1] Web Scraper with BeautifulSoup
items.body:
> 👤 **Assigned Intern:** @sanaayeshakousar2003-arch

## Task Description
Build a web scraper that extracts and saves structured data.

## Requirements
- Scrape a public site (e.g. `books.toscrape.com` or `quotes.toscrape.com`)
- Extract at least 3 fields per item (e.g. title, price, rating)
- Handle pagination (scrape at least 5 pages)
- Save results to a CSV file

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Uses `requests` + `BeautifulSoup4`
- [ ] Handles HTTP errors gracefully (retry on 429/503)
- [ ] Adds a respectful delay between requests (`time.sleep(1)`)
- [ ] Output CSV has a header row and clean data
- [ ] Code is organised into functions (not one big script)

## Resources
- [BeautifulSoup Docs](https://www.crummy.com/software/BeautifulSoup/bs4/doc/)
- [Books to Scrape](https://books.toscrape.com/)

items.title: feat: convert-to-okf support for DOCX / HTML / EPUB

labels.name: difficulty: medium
labels.description: Moderate task requiring familiarity with the project

items.body:
## Background

`scripts/convert-to-okf.py` (the OKF Anything converter) currently covers Markdown lists, JSON, YAML, CSV, key-value text, GitHub URLs, Obsidian/Notion/Feishu/Typora markdown, text-layer PDFs, and prints an OCR recipe for scans.

## Task

Add three more input formats, following the established optional-dependency pattern (like `--format pdf` with pymupdf):

- `--format docx` — extract text via python-docx when installed, else print `pip install python-docx`
- `--format html` — extract readable text via BeautifulSoup when installed, else print `pip install beautifulsoup4`
- `--format epub` — extract chapters via ebooklib when installed, else print `pip install ebooklib`

## Acceptance

- [ ] Each format parses into the intermediate shape (title / url / description + optional body) and renders a myokf-ready bundle
- [ ] Auto-detection by extension (`.docx`, `.html`, `.htm`, `.epub`)
- [ ] A `pytest` test per format (parse + missing-dependency recipe branch)
- [ ] README format table updated in all 4 languages (regenerate via `awesome-okf readme`)

## Reference

See `parse_pdf` in `scripts/convert-to-okf.py` — same pattern, ~20 lines each.

items.title: [bug] BeautifulSoup HTML/EPUB extraction inserts newlines inside inline headings and code tokens
items.body:
## What happened The BeautifulSoup text conversion inserts a newline between **every text node**, including nodes separated only by inline styling. A span inside a heading, word, or syntax-highlighted code block changes the extracted content. This affects two current paths with the same cause: - HTML: the bs4 fallback when Trafilatura is unavailable or does not return usable content. - EPUB: the preferred ebooklib + bs4 parser. This path does not use Trafilatura. On unmodified master, a synthetic two-chapter source using `Chapter 1` produces **0 detected chapters**. Removing only the span markup produces 2. The styled source still exits successfully through the full CLI, including HTML `--mode technical`. For code, this source: ```html 
if enabled:
    print("ok")
``` becomes: ```text if enabled: print ("ok") ``` Compiling that extracted snippet raises `IndentationError`; the same snippet without the styling spans, and the current stdlib output for this fixture, compile successfully. No extracted code was executed. ## What you expected Inline presentation markup should leave text continuous: `Chapter 1: Syntax`, `hypertext`, and the original code lines/indentation. Structural boundaries should still separate headings, paragraphs, lists and table rows; table cells need their own separators. The result should not depend on whether a chapter number or code token is wrapped in an inline element. ## Source document - Formats: synthetic HTML and EPUB 3; English; two content chapters. - No private or copyrighted book was used. - EPUB fixtures include a navigation document. Content manifest order and spine order agree, isolating this from #257. No EPUBCheck conformance result is claimed. - Actual libraries: `beautifulsoup4 4.14.3`, `ebooklib 0.20`; Trafilatura was **absent**, not mocked, in the full CLI reproduction. The HTML trace reported: ```text Trying trafilatura... not available Trying BeautifulSoup (bs4)... OK ``` ## Repro Run the following from the repository root in an environment with BeautifulSoup installed and **without Trafilatura**. This explicitly selects the affected HTML fallback; it does not claim that every successful Trafilatura extraction has this defect. ```python import importlib.util from pathlib import Path from book_to_skill.parsers.html import extract_html_content, _HTMLTextExtractor from book_to_skill.utils import detect_structure assert importlib.util.find_spec("trafilatura") is None raw = ( '' '

Chapter 1: Syntax

' '

A hypertext term remains continuous.

' '

Chapter 2: Safety

' '

Only retry when the failure is temporary.

' '' ) Path("inline-continuity.html").write_text(raw, encoding="utf-8") styled = extract_html_content(raw) plain = extract_html_content(raw.replace("", "").replace("", "")) fallback = _HTMLTextExtractor() fallback.feed(raw) print(repr(styled)) print("styled/control/stdlib chapters:", detect_structure(styled)["chapters_detected"], detect_structure(plain)["chapters_detected"], detect_structure(fallback.get_text())["chapters_detected"]) assert "hyper\ntext" in styled assert detect_structure(styled)["chapters_detected"] == 0 assert detect_structure(plain)["chapters_detected"] == 2 code = '
if enabled:\n    print("ok")\n
' extracted_code = extract_html_content(code) print(repr(extracted_code)) try: compile(extracted_code, "", "exec") except SyntaxError as error: print(type(error).__name__, error.msg) ``` Observed: ```text styled/control/stdlib chapters: 0 2 2 'if enabled:\n \nprint\n("ok")\n' IndentationError expected an indented block after 'if' statement on line 1 ``` The CLI also persists the fragmented heading/word: ```text python scripts/extract.py inline-continuity.html --mode text --install-missing no python scripts/extract.py inline-continuity.html --mode technical --install-missing no ``` Both modes returned 0 and recorded `chapters_detected: 0`, `extraction_method: "html-parser"` in my reproduction. The style-free control returned 0 with 2 detected chapters. Selecting technical mode does not route HTML through the PDF Docling branch. For an independent EPUB reproduction, with real ebooklib installed: ```python from ebooklib import epub from book_to_skill.parsers.epub import extract_with_ebooklib, extract_with_zipfile from book_to_skill.utils import detect_structure book = epub.EpubBook() book.set_identifier("synthetic-inline-continuity") book.set_title("Synthetic continuity") book.set_language("en") chapters = [] for n, title in [(1, "Syntax"), (2, "Safety")]: chapter = epub.EpubHtml(title=title, file_name=f"c{n}.xhtml", lang="en") chapter.content = ( f'

Chapter {n}: {title}

' '

A hypertext term remains continuous.

' ) book.add_item(chapter) chapters.append(chapter) book.toc = tuple(chapters) book.add_item(epub.EpubNav()) book.spine = chapters epub.write_epub("inline-continuity.epub", book) preferred = extract_with_ebooklib("inline-continuity.epub") fallback = extract_with_zipfile("inline-continuity.epub") print("ebooklib/stdlib chapters:", detect_structure(preferred)["chapters_detected"], detect_structure(fallback)["chapters_detected"]) assert "hyper\ntext" in preferred assert detect_structure(preferred)["chapters_detected"] == 0 assert detect_structure(fallback)["chapters_detected"] == 2 ``` Observed: `ebooklib/stdlib chapters: 0 2`. A separate EPUB ZIP fixture with matching manifest/spine order also reproduced this through the unmodified CLI (`extraction_method: "ebooklib"`, 0 chapters). ## Environment and precise source - Windows 11; Python 3.12.14 for independent parser and full CLI reproductions. - book-to-skill 1.4.0, master `c108d25b0cb58e1bdc361f3de02ed9f37075152f`. - BeautifulSoup 4.14.3; ebooklib 0.20; Trafilatura absent. - Repository source remained unchanged. Root cause: - [HTML bs4 conversion](https://github.com/virgiliojr94/book-to-skill/blob/c108d25b0cb58e1bdc361f3de02ed9f37075152f/book_to_skill/parsers/html.py#L121-L128) calls `soup.get_text(separator="\n")`. - [ebooklib conversion](https://github.com/virgiliojr94/book-to-skill/blob/c108d25b0cb58e1bdc361f3de02ed9f37075152f/book_to_skill/parsers/epub.py#L43-L51) uses the same call for each content document. - [Cleanup and structure detection](https://github.com/virgiliojr94/book-to-skill/blob/c108d25b0cb58e1bdc361f3de02ed9f37075152f/book_to_skill/utils.py#L1180-L1221) do not reconstruct inline text. [Corpus serialization](https://github.com/virgiliojr94/book-to-skill/blob/c108d25b0cb58e1bdc361f3de02ed9f37075152f/book_to_skill/utils.py#L1330-L1369) therefore preserves the damaged input. The existing inline continuity tests exercise `_HTMLTextExtractor`, while bs4 convergence checks a table fixture without inline-styled chapter numbers. Those tests can pass while these two production branches fragment inline text. ## Impact Inline spans are used for styled chapter numbers and syntax highlighting. Splitting them can: - remove usable chapter-heading evidence from metadata and later source lookup; - split words or API names, compromising exact search and extraction statistics; - alter code lines/indentation before the generator reads them. This is a demonstrated **input-fidelity defect**. I have not run a live generator and do not claim an observed downstream model failure or a measured prevalence across real books. It also does not imply every code example or every heading is affected: the fixture needs inline text-node boundaries. ## Minimal repair and compatibility Use block-aware HTML-to-text traversal for the bs4/ebooklib conversions: concatenate inline descendants, emit separators at actual block boundaries and `br`, and handle table cells/rows separately. Preserve whitespace verbatim inside `pre/code`. A shared routine could prevent the two paths diverging, provided their existing filtering behavior is preserved explicitly. Do not simply switch to `separator=""`: that can join adjacent blocks and destroy headings/table structure. Do not blindly substitute the current stdlib helper either: it has no preformatted state, and its deferred-boundary whitespace suppression can lose a leading whitespace-only node inside `pre`. Keep EPUB document ordering as a separate concern (#257), keep the existing Trafilatura-first policy, and keep sanitization/path/security checks unchanged. Correctly extracting styled text will intentionally change output bytes, word/token statistics and chapter counts. No new runtime dependency or generator-spec growth is needed. ## Alternatives Until repaired, preconvert the material with a tool that preserves inline/block semantics, or provide a verified plain-text/Markdown version with headings and code intact. The current stdlib path preserves the specific fixtures above, but is not a universal workaround for preformatted whitespace or all HTML structures. Do not strip all markup without first accounting for block boundaries. ## Acceptance and verification limits 1. The styled and style-free fixtures retain identical heading/word text and both report 2 chapters through HTML bs4 and real ebooklib. 2. Syntax-highlighted code retains the same lines/indentation as the source; the nonexecuted compile check succeeds. Include leading spaces before the first highlighted token and multiline nested spans. 3. Adjacent heading/body blocks, explicit `br`, lists and tab-separated table rows retain boundaries; inline `b/i/a/span` and entity decoding do not add separators or double-decode. 4. Existing HTML filtering and EPUB document selection are explicitly regression-tested rather than silently changed. Exercise actual unavailable-Trafilatura fallback and controlled empty/error fallback cases separately. 5. Full CLI tests inspect persisted `full_text.txt` and metadata, not only a text helper. Existing stdlib controls remain covered. Independent direct/parser and CLI checks passed their defect assertions. The existing relevant parser tests also passed **20 tests with 4 skips** in a separate Python 3.14 environment. The four skips were tests gated by `pytest.importorskip("trafilatura")` because that optional package was absent (primary success, empty/whitespace results, and exception); the not-installed fallback case executed. This is not a full-suite pass, a Trafilatura quality evaluation, an EPUBCheck result, or a live model experiment. Deduplication: #107 fixed only stdlib block/inline behavior; #142 introduced Trafilatura and retained this fallback; #235/#251 concern optional-dependency CI coverage; #257 concerns EPUB item order. This report concerns text-node separators with correct item order. I checked all-state issue history and open PRs before submission and found no matching repair for these two conversion calls.

items.title: BeautifulSoup Version
items.body:
### Symptom
`usdm4.utility.soup.get_soup()` logs a Debug entry for most plain-text inputs that contain a `/`:

    Warning raised within Soup package, processing 'Known allergy/ incompatibility against deucravacitinib'
    Message returned 'The input looks more like a filename than markup. You may want to open this file and pass the filehandle into Beautiful Soup.'

Protocol text is full of `and/or`, `U/kg`, `HIV 1/2`, `PaO2/FiO2`, so every protocol gets dozens of these. The same applies to anything else calling `get_soup`, including `tag_resolver.py`.

### Cause
Not a usdm4 code bug. It's the bs4 version.

In beautifulsoup4 <=4.12.x, `_markup_resembles_filename()` treats any string containing `/` or `\` as a possible filename. From 4.13 it only warns when the text ends in `.html`, `.htm`, `.xml`, `.xhtml` or `.txt` and passes further filename checks.

Checked against real criteria text:

| Text | 4.12.3 | 4.13.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `Known allergy/ incompatibility` | warns | quiet |
| `have >1.2 U/kg` | warns | quiet |
| `plain text` | quiet | quiet |

usdm4 declares `beautifulsoup4>=4.9` in `setup.py` and `requirements.txt`. That floor lets existing environments stay on 4.12.x.

### Fix
- `setup.py`: change `"beautifulsoup4>=4.9"` to `"beautifulsoup4>=4.13.1"`
- `requirements.txt`: same change
- Use 4.13.1, not 4.13.0. 4.13.0 was yanked from PyPI (wrong minimum Python pin).

`get_soup()` itself doesn't change. It should keep logging whatever warnings bs4 raises. Only the false positives go away.

### Checks
- Run the full test suite on bs4 >=4.13.1. 4.13 was a large release (type hints, some API tidy-up). Any usage of deprecated bs4 APIs should show up as failures or DeprecationWarnings.
- Any expected-error fixtures that captured the `get_soup` Debug entries will need regenerating.

### Related
usdm4_fhir issue #41 adds `beautifulsoup4>=4.13.1` to usdm4_fhir directly, since it imports bs4 itself.
